name: Workforce Capacity Planner
description: A Power BI custom visual for modelling workforce capacity, FTE scenarios, utilization, demand gaps, and cost impact by department and position role.
shortDescription: Model demand, FTE, productivity, capacity gaps, utilization, and cost impact directly inside Power BI.
whatItDoesTitle: A focused planner for staffing scenarios inside Power BI.
whatItDoesText: Workforce Capacity Planner compares demand against current and scenario capacity by department and position role. Report users can add or remove FTE by role and immediately see how capacity, gap, utilization, required FTE, and cost impact change.
fieldRolesTitle: Inputs aligned to workforce capacity planning.
formattingControlsTitle: Controls for executive and planner layouts.
howToUseTitle: Map demand and staffing fields, then test scenarios.
useCasesTitle: Built for teams planning operational staffing.
ctaTitle: Start modelling workforce capacity in Power BI.
ctaText: Download the free MVP package and sample data to test Capacity Planner in Power BI Desktop.

fieldRoles.name: Position Role
fieldRoles.description: Staffing role such as Officer, Supervisor, Agent, Admin, or Analyst.

fieldRoles.name: Demand Volume
fieldRoles.description: Number of workload units in the selected period.

fieldRoles.name: Productivity per FTE
fieldRoles.description: Demand units one FTE can complete in the selected period.

fieldRoles.name: Current FTE
fieldRoles.description: Current number of FTEs available.

fieldRoles.name: Department
fieldRoles.description: Service line, program, queue, or department. When omitted, rows are grouped under Unassigned department.

fieldRoles.name: Cost per FTE
fieldRoles.description: Estimated cost per FTE used for current cost, scenario cost, and cost impact.

formattingControls: Layout modes: Compact, Executive, and Full planner.
Show or hide title, subtitle, executive cards, interpretation panel, and table.
Configure table density, sticky header, and maximum visible rows.
Customize card style, colors, bar style, font, spacing, and number formatting.
Premium mode enables demand shock modelling and advanced customization controls.

features.title: Scenario FTE Controls
features.does: Adds or removes FTE by position role and clamps negative scenario FTE to zero.
features.matters: Lets report users test staffing tradeoffs without changing the underlying dataset.

features.title: Capacity and Gap Calculations
features.does: Calculates current capacity, scenario capacity, demand gap, required FTE, and utilization.
features.matters: Turns operational staffing assumptions into a direct capacity signal.

features.title: Cost Impact
features.does: Shows current cost, scenario cost, and cost impact when Cost per FTE is bound.
features.matters: Adds a financial view without requiring cost data for teams that only need capacity modelling.

features.title: Capacity and Cost Views
features.does: Splits the detail table into focused operational and cost views.
features.matters: Reduces cognitive load compared with a single wide table.

features.title: Interpretation Panel
features.does: Generates deterministic plain-language scenario interpretation inside the visual.
features.matters: Helps executives and analysts explain the scenario without calling an external AI service.

features.title: Client-Side MVP
features.does: Runs in Power BI without backend services, external APIs, writeback, authentication, or persistence.
features.matters: Keeps the first version simple to test, review, and govern.

steps: Import the Workforce Capacity Planner .pbiviz package into Power BI Desktop.
Add the visual to a report page.
Map Position Role, Demand Volume, Productivity per FTE, and Current FTE.
Optionally map Department and Cost per FTE.
Use the role steppers to add or remove FTE and review the recalculated summary, table, and interpretation.

name: RouteOps Visual
description: A Power BI custom visual for mapping and analyzing vehicles, deliveries, mobile assets, service stops, depots, routes, and operational exceptions using data already available in a Power BI model.
shortDescription: Track vehicles, deliveries, mobile assets, stops, and operational exceptions directly inside Power BI.
whatItDoesTitle: An operational map for fleet, delivery, and field-service visibility.
whatItDoesText: RouteOps renders the latest location per entity on an SVG/D3 map, supports route and delivery context fields, and highlights operational exceptions such as stale GPS, offline assets, idle vehicles, delayed or failed deliveries, overdue work, delivery-window breaches, and SLA breaches.
featuresTitle: Designed for operations teams watching mobile work.
fieldRolesTitle: Inputs aligned to route and delivery operations.
formattingControlsTitle: Controls for map density, exceptions, and premium overlays.
howToUseTitle: Map operational locations, then review exceptions.
useCasesTitle: Built for teams monitoring movement and service execution.
ctaTitle: Start mapping route operations in Power BI.
ctaText: Download the RouteOps visual package and sample fleet delivery data to test operational mapping in Power BI Desktop.

fieldRoles.name: Entity ID
fieldRoles.description: Stable vehicle, asset, delivery, order, package, stop, or service-call identifier.

fieldRoles.name: Latitude
fieldRoles.description: WGS84 latitude for the entity, vehicle, asset, delivery, or stop location.

fieldRoles.name: Longitude
fieldRoles.description: WGS84 longitude for the entity, vehicle, asset, delivery, or stop location.

fieldRoles.name: Timestamp
fieldRoles.description: GPS, delivery, stop, or operational event timestamp used to identify latest positions.

fieldRoles.name: Status
fieldRoles.description: Operational status used for marker color, exception visibility, and summary badges.

fieldRoles.name: Route and delivery context
fieldRoles.description: Route ID, driver, depot, region, delivery ID, order ID, stop sequence, ETA, scheduled time, delivery window, SLA, and exception fields.

formattingControls: Show latest entity locations with auto-zoom, labels, SVG tooltips, and summary badges.
Configure status colors, marker visibility, stale GPS, offline, idle, overdue, failed delivery, and delivery-window exception logic.
Use free/premium gates for route trails, playback hooks, geofences, sequencing, route deviation, SLA highlighting, heatmaps, and advanced exception views.
Render the MVP without external map tiles, API keys, telemetry, or custom backend calls.

features.title: Latest Location Map
features.does: Shows the latest point for vehicles, assets, deliveries, stops, depots, and other mobile entities.
features.matters: Keeps operational location awareness inside the same Power BI reports teams already use.

features.title: Operational Exception Logic
features.does: Flags stale GPS, offline assets, idle vehicles, delayed deliveries, failed deliveries, overdue work, delivery-window breaches, and SLA breaches.
features.matters: Helps teams move from raw telemetry rows to the exceptions that need attention.

features.title: Route and Delivery Context
features.does: Accepts route, driver, stop, depot, warehouse, region, ETA, scheduled time, delivery window, and destination fields.
features.matters: Lets one visual support fleet, courier, field-service, logistics, and mobile asset use cases.

features.title: No-Tile SVG Map MVP
features.does: Renders a local SVG/D3 geospatial canvas without external map tiles or map-provider API keys.
features.matters: Keeps operational data inside the Power BI visual sandbox for privacy-sensitive evaluation.

features.title: Freemium Operations Layer
features.does: Provides core marker, label, tooltip, summary, and exception views in free mode, with premium hooks for trails, playback, geofences, sequencing, heatmaps, and advanced monitoring.
features.matters: Creates a useful entry point while leaving room for deeper operational analytics.

steps: Import the RouteOps Visual for Power BI .pbiviz package into Power BI Desktop.
Add the visual to a report page.
Map Entity ID, Latitude, Longitude, and Timestamp.
Optionally map Status, Route ID, Driver Name, Delivery ID, Stop Sequence, ETA, delivery-window, destination, and exception fields.
Review latest locations, summary badges, tooltips, and operational exception markers.

name: Product Margin What-If Cards
fullName: Product Margin What-If Cards (Power BI Visual)
description: A Power BI custom visual for modelling product-level price, input costs, unit margin, break-even units, and profit impact with interactive what-if scenario cards.
shortDescription: Model product price, input costs, margin, and per-unit profit scenarios directly inside Power BI.
whatItDoesTitle: A compact what-if model for product unit economics.
whatItDoesText: Product Margin What-If Cards turns product price, unit cost, and individual cost inputs into scenario cards. Report users can adjust selling price and per-unit input costs, then immediately see how unit cost, unit margin, margin percent, break-even units, and profit impact change.
formattingControlsTitle: Controls for scenario cards and SKU visuals.
howToUseTitle: Map product economics, then adjust assumptions.
useCasesTitle: Built for teams managing product profitability.
ctaTitle: Start modelling product margin scenarios in Power BI.
ctaText: Download the free Product Margin What-If Cards package and sample data to test per-unit scenario analysis in Power BI Desktop.

fieldRoles.name: Product Name
fieldRoles.description: Product, SKU, item, or service name used to render one card per product.

fieldRoles.name: Selling Price
fieldRoles.description: Baseline selling price per unit before scenario adjustments.

fieldRoles.name: Unit Cost
fieldRoles.description: Baseline total unit cost used when detailed Cost Inputs are not mapped.

fieldRoles.name: Cost Inputs
fieldRoles.description: Per-unit cost components such as material, packaging, shipping, labour, platform fee, advertising, tax, or other inputs.

fieldRoles.name: Product Image
fieldRoles.description: SKU image supplied as an HTTPS image URL, data URL, or base64 image value.

fieldRoles.name: Fixed Costs
fieldRoles.description: Fixed cost assumption used for break-even units when premium features are enabled.

formattingControls: Configure card count, card size, spacing, image visibility, and compact, standard, or detailed layouts.
Adjust scenario selling price and individual input costs with visual-level sliders.
Show or hide core metrics, premium outputs, break-even units, scenario comparison, sensitivity analysis, and KPI cards.
Use conditional color feedback for positive and negative margin impact.
Render SKU image URLs from the Product Image field or fall back to data/base64 images and placeholders.

features.title: Per-Unit Scenario Cards
features.does: Renders product cards with baseline and scenario selling price, unit cost, unit margin, margin percent, and profit impact.
features.matters: Keeps product profitability modelling close to the report context instead of pushing analysts into a spreadsheet.

features.title: Individual Cost Input Sliders
features.does: Lets report users adjust mapped input costs such as material, shipping, labour, fees, advertising, and tax independently.
features.matters: Shows which assumption is actually moving unit margin rather than treating cost as one opaque number.

features.title: Live Margin Feedback
features.does: Updates KPI cards, scenario values, cost split bars, and positive or negative color feedback as assumptions change.
features.matters: Makes margin pressure visible while users are still exploring the scenario.

features.title: Premium-Ready Analysis
features.does: Includes gated premium paths for more product cards, more cost inputs, break-even units, target margin price solving, scenario comparison, and sensitivity analysis.
features.matters: Supports a useful free tier today while leaving room for advanced monetized workflows.

features.title: SKU Image Support
features.does: Displays product imagery from HTTPS URLs, data URLs, base64 image values, or a branded placeholder fallback.
features.matters: Helps commercial and ecommerce teams recognize products quickly in dense report pages.

features.title: Client-Side Visual
features.does: Runs scenario calculations inside the Power BI visual runtime without Zaratuk backend services, writeback, or scenario persistence.
features.matters: Keeps the MVP straightforward for teams that want to test the visual inside governed Power BI reports.

steps: Import the Product Margin What-If Cards .pbiviz package into Power BI Desktop.
Add the visual to a report page.
Map Product Name, Selling Price, and either Unit Cost or one or more Cost Inputs.
Optionally map Product ID, Category, Product Image, and Fixed Costs.
Use the scenario sliders to adjust selling price and input costs, then review margin, break-even, and profit impact.

name: Data Health Panel
description: A Power BI custom visual that evaluates whether data can be trusted by showing a weighted 0-100 health score, four quality KPI tiles, and a plain-English diagnostic issue list.
shortDescription: Score completeness, freshness, uniqueness, and category validity directly inside Power BI reports.
whatItDoesTitle: A clear signal for the health of the data behind the report.
whatItDoesText: Data Health Panel evaluates selected fields across completeness, freshness, uniqueness, and category validity. It gives teams a concise health score, focused quality indicators, and diagnostic issues without turning the report page into a troubleshooting maze.
howToUseTitle: Add the visual, map the fields, review the signal.
useCasesTitle: Built for teams responsible for trusted data.
ctaTitle: Add a trust signal to your report data.
ctaText: Download the current Data Health Panel package for free. Documentation and Microsoft AppSource slots are prepared for the production release path.

fieldRoles.name: Fields to Check Completeness
fieldRoles.description: Fields where blanks or nulls reduce the completeness score.

fieldRoles.name: Fields to Check Uniqueness
fieldRoles.description: Identifier fields where repeated values reduce the uniqueness score.

fieldRoles.name: Field to Check Freshness
fieldRoles.description: A date field used to evaluate how old the dataset is.

fieldRoles.name: Fields to Validate Categories
fieldRoles.description: Category fields checked for blanks, low-frequency values, and fragmentation.

formattingControls: Show or hide the health score, KPI tiles, and issue list.
Adjust base font size for report layouts.
Configure fresh hours, stale hours, blank thresholds, low-frequency thresholds, fragmentation thresholds, and row limits.
Override good, warning, and bad score colors.

features.title: Weighted Data Health Score
features.does: Computes a 0-100 score from completeness, freshness, uniqueness, and validity using intent-driven Power BI field buckets.
features.matters: Gives report users a single trust signal before they interpret operational metrics.

features.title: Completeness Checks
features.does: Measures the average percent of non-blank values across fields selected for completeness.
features.matters: Makes missing values visible inside the Power BI report instead of hiding quality checks in a separate workflow.

features.title: Freshness Evaluation
features.does: Compares the latest selected date against fresh and stale hour thresholds.
features.matters: Helps IT and BI teams see when a Power BI report is relying on stale operational data.

features.title: Uniqueness Detection
features.does: Calculates distinct-value rates and flags duplicate identifier values, with row limits for distinct-count performance.
features.matters: Reduces duplicate-driven reporting errors such as double counting cases, tickets, or transactions.

features.title: Category Validity Review
features.does: Checks category fields for blanks, low-frequency categories, and high fragmentation.
features.matters: Surfaces operational taxonomy issues that can make filters, slicers, and status dashboards harder to trust.

features.title: Plain-English Issue List
features.does: Ranks diagnostic messages by severity and links issues to the related quality dimension.
features.matters: Turns quality scoring into actionable report feedback for analysts, BI developers, and operations teams.

steps: Import the Data Health Panel .pbiviz package into Power BI Desktop.
Add Data Health Panel to the report canvas.
Assign fields into the intent-driven buckets: completeness, uniqueness, freshness, and category validity.
Tune display, threshold, and color settings from the Power BI formatting pane.
Review the health score, KPI tiles, and diagnostic issue list directly in the report.

name: Pipeline Health Monitor
description: A Power BI custom visual that monitors pipeline run health by showing latest status, duration, SLA health, anomaly warnings, and duration trends for operational datasets.
shortDescription: Monitor pipeline status, duration, SLA health, and basic anomalies directly inside Power BI.
scoreFormula: Latest Duration > Average Prior Completed Duration x 1.5
whatItDoesTitle: A compact operational view of pipeline health inside Power BI.
whatItDoesText: Pipeline Health Monitor groups raw pipeline run rows by pipeline, identifies the latest run by maximum start time, and shows current status, run duration, optional SLA status, duration trend, and basic anomaly warnings without leaving the Power BI report canvas.
fieldRolesTitle: Field roles aligned to pipeline run telemetry.
howToUseTitle: Map run fields, then review pipeline health.
useCasesTitle: Built for teams watching operational pipelines.
ctaTitle: Add pipeline health monitoring to Power BI.
ctaText: Download the free Pipeline Health Monitor package and use the sample pipeline run data to test status, duration, SLA, and anomaly behavior inside Power BI.

fieldRoles.name: Pipeline Name
fieldRoles.description: Pipeline, job, workflow, or process name used to group run history.

fieldRoles.name: Run ID
fieldRoles.description: Unique run identifier. Duplicate Run IDs are deduplicated per pipeline.

fieldRoles.name: Status
fieldRoles.description: Raw run status text. Matching is case-insensitive and supports partial values such as SUCCESS, FAILED - timeout, and In Progress.

fieldRoles.name: Start Time
fieldRoles.description: Run start timestamp. Rows without Start Time are ignored.

fieldRoles.name: End Time
fieldRoles.description: Run end timestamp. Blank End Time is treated as Running.

fieldRoles.name: Expected Completion Time
fieldRoles.description: Optional SLA timestamp. When omitted, the SLA Status column is hidden.

formattingControls: Configure success, failure, and running status colors.
Show or hide the duration sparkline.
Enable compact mode for dense operational report layouts.

features.title: Latest Run Health
features.does: Groups runs by pipeline and identifies the latest run using the maximum Start Time.
features.matters: Gives Power BI users a current operational signal for each pipeline instead of forcing them to scan raw run logs.

features.title: Status Normalization
features.does: Interprets common success, failure, running, and unknown status values from raw text.
features.matters: Keeps pipeline health readable even when upstream tools use slightly different status labels.

features.title: Duration and Trend Sparkline
features.does: Shows latest duration and a compact sparkline for the last five runs by duration.
features.matters: Helps teams see whether a pipeline is slowing down before it becomes a visible reporting issue.

features.title: SLA Status
features.does: Displays On Time or Late when Expected Completion Time is mapped.
features.matters: Turns Power BI into a practical surface for monitoring operational reporting commitments.

features.title: Basic Anomaly Warning
features.does: Flags the latest run when its duration is more than 1.5 times the average prior completed duration.
features.matters: Surfaces performance drift directly inside reports without requiring a separate monitoring tool.

features.title: Duplicate Run Deduplication
features.does: Deduplicates repeated Run IDs per pipeline before evaluating the latest status and duration.
features.matters: Reduces noise from duplicate ingestion or repeated updates in pipeline telemetry tables.

steps: Import the Pipeline Health Monitor .pbiviz package into Power BI Desktop.
Add Pipeline Health Monitor to the report canvas.
Map Pipeline Name, Run ID, Status, Start Time, and End Time fields.
Optionally map Expected Completion Time to enable SLA Status.
Review latest status, duration, SLA health, anomaly warnings, and duration trends directly in the report.

name: LLM Usage Monitor
fullName: LLM Usage Monitor (Power BI Custom Connector)
description: A beta Power BI custom connector for LLM usage monitoring that helps analysts track organization-level token usage, model consumption, request volume, and cost across OpenAI and Anthropic admin APIs.
shortDescription: Monitor LLM token usage, model consumption, requests, and cost in Power BI with a beta custom connector.
whatItDoesTitle: A Power BI connector for the token and cost data behind AI usage.
whatItDoesText: LLM Usage Monitor is a beta connector that brings organization-level LLM usage APIs into Power BI as clean tables for usage, costs, models, API keys, projects, and service tiers. It is designed for analysts who need to explain where AI consumption is coming from, which models drive cost, and how usage changes over time.
featuresTitle: Designed to make LLM usage visible in Power BI.
fieldRolesTitle: Inputs and tables aligned to LLM operations.
howToUseTitle: Install the connector, choose a provider, then load usage tables.
useCasesTitle: Built for teams responsible for AI usage visibility.
ctaTitle: Start monitoring LLM usage from Power BI.
ctaText: Download the free beta LLM Usage Monitor .mez connector and follow the documentation to add it to your Power BI custom connector folder.

securityScan.summary: The LLMUsageConnector repository scan reported 0 issues across monitored security checks.
securityScan.note: This scan is a helpful third-party signal for the repository, but it does not replace your organization's own review of beta software, connector behavior, and credential handling.

checks.name: Open source dependency monitoring
checks.description: Monitors third-party dependencies and lockfiles for known vulnerabilities.

checks.name: Exposed secrets monitoring
checks.description: Checks whether secrets have been accidentally exposed in the source repository.

checks.name: License management
checks.description: Reviews dependency licenses for usage and compliance concerns.

checks.name: SAST
checks.description: Runs static application security testing on the connector code.

checks.name: Infrastructure as Code
checks.description: Checks infrastructure-as-code files where monitored files are present.

checks.name: Supply-chain malware
checks.description: Checks dependencies for known malicious package signals.

checks.name: Mobile issues
checks.description: Checks mobile manifest issues where monitored mobile files are present.

checks.name: GitHub access control issues
checks.description: Monitors repository access and source-code security controls.

fieldRoles.name: Provider
fieldRoles.description: Select OpenAI (Organization Admin API) or Anthropic (Organization Admin API only) from the connector prompt.

fieldRoles.name: Admin API Key
fieldRoles.description: Use an organization admin key with access to usage and cost reporting APIs. Standard runtime API keys are not enough.

fieldRoles.name: Usage Tables
fieldRoles.description: Load Usage, Costs, Models, UsageByApiKey, UsageByProject, and UsageByServiceTier into Power BI.

features.title: Daily Usage and Cost Tables
features.does: Exposes daily token usage, request volume, and cost as typed Power BI tables.
features.matters: Gives analysts a reliable model for tracking LLM usage without manually exporting billing screens or API reports.

features.title: Provider Selection
features.does: Supports OpenAI organization admin APIs and Anthropic organization admin APIs from one connector entry point.
features.matters: Lets Power BI reports compare usage patterns across supported LLM providers while keeping provider-specific API details behind the connector.

features.title: Model-Level Visibility
features.does: Breaks usage down by model with input tokens, output tokens, total tokens, and requests.
features.matters: Helps teams see which models are driving adoption and cost instead of treating LLM spend as one blended number.

features.title: API Key, Project, and Service Tier Views
features.does: Provides separate tables for usage by API key, provider project, and service tier when the provider API returns those dimensions.
features.matters: Supports chargeback, operational review, and governance workflows for teams managing shared AI infrastructure.

features.title: Power BI Credential Store Authentication
features.does: Uses Power BI Key authentication so provider admin keys are entered through the credential prompt instead of stored in source files.
features.matters: Keeps sensitive credentials out of reports, connector code, and documentation.

features.title: Refresh-Oriented Connector Design
features.does: Uses a stable data source kind, static base URLs, relative paths, typed schemas, and retry handling for common transient API failures.
features.matters: Makes the connector easier to operate in Power BI workflows that need repeatable refresh behavior.

steps: Download the LLMUsageMonitor.mez connector package.
Copy the .mez file into Documents\Microsoft Power BI Desktop\Custom Connectors.
Restart Power BI Desktop and enable custom connectors under Security options if required.
Open Get Data, search for LLM Token Usage, and select the connector.
Choose OpenAI or Anthropic as the provider and paste the matching organization Admin API key.
Load the usage, cost, model, API key, project, and service tier tables needed for your report.
